title: Balconies, Canopies and Awnings Projecting Over the Street: QCVN 01:2026
desc: How far may townhouse balconies, canopies and awnings project? QCVN 01:2026 principles on projecting architectural details, red lines, setbacks and neighbors.
summary: QCVN 01:2026/BXD (effective 1 January 2027) sets principles for balconies, canopies and awnings projecting past the building line; specific projections are set by detailed planning and local architectural regulations.
body: p

Balconies, canopies and awnings add beauty to a townhouse facade but also often cause disputes when they project over the sidewalk or into the neighboring house. From 1 January 2027, QCVN 01:2026/BXD replaces QCVN 01:2021/BXD (Article 2 of Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD). This article summarizes the principles homeowners should know before designing the facade.
h2
1. Three concepts to understand
p
Under Section 1.4 of QCVN 01:2026:
ul
Red line (road boundary): the boundary between land on which buildings may be built and land reserved for roads, technical infrastructure or public space.
Building line: the limit within which a building is permitted to be built above ground.
Setback: the space between the red line and the building line.
p
These two lines for your land plot are recorded in the planning information – see How to obtain planning information before buying land or building a house.
h2
2. Houses with no setback (built right at the sidewalk)
p
When the building line coincides with the red line, architectural details projecting past the building line must (Section 2.5.7.1):
ul
Not obstruct traffic on the roadway;
Ensure safety and convenience for pedestrians on the sidewalk;
Not affect the greenery or the above-ground and underground technical infrastructure along the route;
Ensure uniformity of the streetscape along the street or street section;
Comply with fire prevention and fighting requirements and not obstruct firefighting vehicles.
h2
3. Houses with a setback
p

When the building line is set back from the red line, details projecting past the building line must not extend beyond the red line, must keep the streetscape consistent and comply with fire prevention and fighting requirements (Section 2.5.7.2). In existing areas that cannot meet the common setback, the setback may be determined separately in detailed planning or urban design (Section 2.6.4).
h2
4. How many meters may it project?
p

QCVN 01:2026 does not give a single general figure for the projection of balconies and canopies. The regulation provides that architectural details adjoining traffic roads are set by detailed planning, urban design and architectural management regulations in each area, while also ensuring the principles above (Section 2.5.7). Therefore, before designing, you need to look at the architectural management regulations or detailed planning of the area – see How architectural management regulations affect house building.
h2
5. The side adjoining the neighboring house
p

Architectural details at the part adjoining the neighboring building must not cross the boundary of the land plot (when the two houses are on two different plots), must comply with fire prevention and fighting requirements, and must not adversely affect the daily life of the neighboring building (Section 2.5.8). For example, canopies, gutters or air-conditioner outdoor units reaching over the neighbor's roof are not allowed.
h2
6. Do canopies and awnings count toward building density?
p

Gutters, canopies, eaves, awnings, entrance steps, sills and the like that comply with fire safety and construction safety requirements are not counted in the site coverage area if they do not obstruct the circulation of people and vehicles and are not combined with another use (Note 2 of Section 1.4.19). A balcony used as a seating area or for drying laundry, or a canopy that has been “extended” into a room, is no longer a decorative detail. On building density, see Building density and setbacks for houses under QCVN 01:2026.
p

note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace legal documents. QCVN 01:2026/BXD is effective from 1 January 2027; plans approved earlier continue to be implemented until the end of their term (Section 5.4). Specific projections are set by detailed planning, urban design and the architectural management regulations of each locality – ask the commune- or ward-level People's Committee before designing.
